findings.claim: Food must be fully thawed before cooking.
findings.truth: Food normally needs thorough defrosting, but it may be cooked from frozen when the manufacturer’s instructions say so or a proven safe method is used.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, Safe Catering defrosting guidance (fetched)

findings.claim: The vast majority of the estimated 2.4 million UK food-borne illnesses are caused by bacterial contamination.
findings.truth: The FSA estimate includes illness caused by bacteria, viruses and other pathogens; its model includes a large number of unattributed cases.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, The Burden of Foodborne Disease in the UK 2018 (fetched)

findings.claim: The legal safe core temperature for cooked food in the UK is 75°C at the centre.
findings.truth: 75°C for 30 seconds is one FSA safe cooking combination; other safe temperature-time combinations are also given, so there is not one legal temperature stated this way.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency, Cooking your food, temperature-time guidance (fetched)

findings.claim: The specification also acknowledges Listeria, Bacillus cereus and Clostridium species in this food-safety content.
findings.truth: The specification names Salmonella, Campylobacter, E. coli and Staphylococcus in its food-poisoning content; it does not name those additional bacteria there.

findings.claim: The FSA estimates household food waste costs the average family around £700 per year.
findings.truth: WRAP’s 2022 estimate is about £1,000 of food and drink wasted per household of four; it is not an FSA estimate.
findings.evidence: WRAP, Household Food and Drink Waste in the UK 2022 (fetched)

findings.claim: UK households throw away approximately 6.7 million tonnes of food every year.
findings.truth: WRAP estimates that UK households wasted around 6.0 million tonnes of food and drink in 2022.
findings.evidence: WRAP, Household Food and Drink Waste in the UK 2022 (fetched)

findings.claim: Around 735 million people globally were experiencing hunger as of recent WHO estimates.
findings.truth: The latest SOFI estimate available at checking was 645 million people facing hunger in 2025.

findings.claim: West Country cooking features Stilton cheese.
findings.truth: Stilton is protected for production in Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire; Cheddar is an appropriate West Country example.
findings.evidence: DEFRA, Stilton Blue Cheese product specification (fetched)

findings.claim: The ASA restricts HFSS adverts before 9 pm or on platforms primarily used by under-16s.
findings.truth: UK-wide restrictions in force from 5 January 2026 prohibit advertising less healthy food or drink on TV before 9 pm and paid-for advertising online at any time.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Applying the new NPM to advertising and promotions restrictions (fetched)

findings.claim: The lesson presents the specification’s definition of cuisine as a quotation-like definition.
findings.truth: The wording tracks the specification closely. Keep future instructional text paraphrased rather than reproducing board wording.

summary: Nine surgical corrections were verified across five lessons. One low-severity copyright-distancing note needs no edit.
